page.kotlinDsl.concepts.naming.text.message: Each component has a function named after its class in camelCase. Most take the options you set most often, such as a label or a placeholder, before the block.

page.kotlinDsl.concepts.nesting.text.message: Components that hold children accept nested DSL calls inside their block, so the code has the shape of the screen.

page.kotlinDsl.concepts.events.text.message: Listeners use on prefixed methods that take a lambda, such as onClick and onModify.

page.kotlinDsl.concepts.scope.text.message: Children only go into components that support them. Adding to an outer scope by accident does not compile.

page.kotlinDsl.concepts.styles.text.message: The styles property gives bracket access to CSS properties, the same as setStyle() in Java. Class names are added with +=.

page.kotlinDsl.concepts.java.text.message: Kotlin compiles to JVM bytecode. Use Kotlin composites from Java classes and nest Java components in DSL blocks with add().

page.kotlinDsl.start.steps.dependency.te.message: Add the webforJ Kotlin DSL module and the Kotlin standard library to your pom.xml.

page.kotlinDsl.start.steps.plugin.text.message: It compiles your Kotlin and Java sources in one build. No separate Kotlin installation is needed.

page.kotlinDsl.start.steps.files.title.message: Put Kotlin next to your Java

page.kotlinDsl.start.steps.files.text.message: Kotlin files can go in their own source folder or in the same folder as your Java files.

page.kotlinDsl.start.steps.view.text.message: Write a view with the builders. Maven then compiles your Kotlin alongside your Java.

page.kotlinDsl.hero.lead.message: The Kotlin DSL builds webforJ UIs with concise, type-safe syntax. Instead of imperative calls, you write declarative code that reads like a description of the screen, and it compiles in the same project as your Java.

page.kotlinDsl.names.title.message: The class you know, as a builder

page.kotlinDsl.names.note.message: Buttons, fields, layouts, dialogs, drawers, lists and HTML elements each have one, named after the class in camelCase.

page.kotlinDsl.compare.lead.message: Both sides build the same components with the same webforJ classes. The Kotlin side drops the setters and add() calls: components nest inside each other and configuration happens in blocks.

page.kotlinDsl.concepts.lead.message: Each builder function creates a component, adds it to its parent container and runs a configuration block. The rest of the DSL follows from that.

page.kotlinDsl.concepts.blocks.text.message: The block receives the component as {code}, so you set its properties and call its methods directly.

page.kotlinDsl.extend.short.message: Custom components and third-party libraries join the DSL through an extension function on {hasComponents}. The {init} helper adds the component to its parent, runs the block and returns it. Composites you build with the DSL get a function the same way.

page.kotlinDsl.extend.link.message: Extending the DSL in the docs

page.mcpApps.flow.step1Text.message: The host calls the {tool} tool, with input such as a warehouse code.

page.mcpApps.flow.step2Text.message: webforJ renders the routed view {route}, and the view opens in the conversation.

page.mcpApps.flow.step4Text.message: The view sends messages and model context back to the conversation.

page.mcpApps.host.contextText.message: {call} replaces the context the view contributes to the model. Later responses can use it, and no visible message is added.

page.mcpApps.host.eventsText.message: Listeners such as {cancelled} and {changed} let the view react when a tool call is cancelled or the conversation context changes.

page.mcpApps.host.leaveText.message: {link} continues on an external page, and {mode} asks for a different presentation. The host decides whether it can satisfy either request.

page.mcpApps.run.standardText.message: An initializer scans the package of the routed views, contributes their tools and UI resources to an MCP server, and mounts Streamable HTTP at {path}. One {install} call adds the embed support the host needs.

page.mcpApps.test.baseline1.message: The client connects to the MCP endpoint.

page.mcpApps.open.lead.message: Add {app} to a routed view and it is published as a tool. The description tells the AI when the tool is useful. One object type, such as an {record} record, describes the arguments, and an {input} method applies them after the route renders.

page.mcpApps.open.namesText.message: Without {name}, webforJ derives the tool name from the route: {route} becomes {tool}, {nestedRoute} becomes {nestedTool}, and the root route becomes {rootTool}.

page.mcpApps.open.modeText.message: {mode} asks the host how to present the view. The host can choose a different mode.

page.mcpApps.change.lead.message: These tools do not open the app. A call goes to the rendered {tool} view in the same MCP session. If that view is not open, the call returns an error that directs the host to call {tool} first.

page.mcpApps.change.actionTitle.message: An action is a view method

page.mcpApps.change.actionText.message: Add {annotation} to a method and it becomes a tool with its own input. The method name {method} produces {tool}.

page.mcpApps.change.updateTitle.message: One update tool with the opening input

page.mcpApps.change.updateText.message: A view that implements {observer} gets one update tool with the same input schema as {tool}. The callback decides how to use the arguments and returns the tool result.

page.mcpApps.change.updatePoint1.message: webforJ does not apply the values to components automatically.

page.mcpApps.change.updatePoint2.message: Calling it does not open the route or render another view.

page.mcpApps.change.updatePoint3.message: The update tool has no UI resource metadata.

page.mcpApps.change.updatePoint4.message: A view can use both an action and the update tool.

page.mcpApps.host.lead.message: The same route also opens in a normal browser, so each host interaction starts by checking that a host is present. Host calls are asynchronous and return a {result}.

page.modernization.phases.p1.title.message: Run the desktop app in the browser

page.modernization.phases.p1.text.message: Webswing runs your Swing, JavaFX or SWT app on the server and streams its interface to the browser as HTML5 canvas. Mouse and keyboard input go back to the real app. The source code does not change.

page.modernization.phases.p1.note.message: Embed it in a webforJ view with WebswingConnector. The connector connects to the Webswing server when it is added to the page.

page.modernization.phases.p2.text.message: New screens are written in webforJ and sit next to the embedded app. The two sides send each other actions, so a click in Swing can open a web form and a save on the web updates the Swing table. Users work in old and new screens in the same browser tab.

page.modernization.phases.p2.note.message: Swing announces a double click as select-customer. webforJ opens its own form and sends update-customer back on save.

page.modernization.phases.p3.text.message: Replace the Swing screens one at a time, in the order that matters to your business. When a screen has a webforJ equivalent, delete its actions. After the last one, the Webswing layer and the desktop client go away.

page.modernization.phases.p3.runs.desc.message: One Java app in the browser, every screen written in webforJ.

page.modernization.phases.p3.goes.desc.message: The Webswing server, the streamed desktop UI and the installed client.

page.modernization.phases.p3.stays.desc.message: Your domain classes, services and validation rules, called from the new screens as Java methods.

page.modernization.phases.p3.note.message: You can stop after any phase and still have gained something. Phase 2 can run for as long as the budget allows.

page.modernization.stays.team.text.message: The people who maintain the Swing app today build the web screens in Java. There is no second team and no front-end toolchain to learn.

page.modernization.stays.code.text.message: Webswing runs the app as it is. The same code base keeps working as a desktop app and in the browser, so you maintain one app, not two.

page.modernization.stays.logic.text.message: Domain classes, services and validation rules that have nothing to do with {code} are called straight from the new screens. They do not become endpoints first.

page.modernization.stays.toolchain.text.message: Maven, your IDE, your debugger and your existing tests continue to apply.

page.modernization.ai.loop.one.text.message: Ask for the webforJ equivalent that calls your existing services.

page.modernization.ai.loop.two.text.message: The MCP server looks up webforJ documentation and API details on demand, instead of guessing.

page.modernization.ai.loop.three.text.message: Compare behavior against the Swing original, then move on to the next screen.

page.modernization.hero.caption.message: A double click in the Swing table opens a webforJ dialog instead of the old Swing one. Both run in the same browser tab.

page.modernization.hero.lead.message: Your Swing, JavaFX or SWT app runs in a web browser without changes to its source. Then you build new screens in webforJ around it and replace the old ones at your own pace. The Java team and the code stay.

page.modernization.hero.fact1.message: Desktop toolkits: Swing, JavaFX and SWT

page.modernization.hero.fact2.message: Source changes to run in a browser

page.modernization.stays.lead.message: webforJ is the full-stack Java framework for business web apps: you build the whole app, screens included, in Java. So moving a Swing app means moving its screens, and everything under them carries over.

page.modernization.stays.changesText.message: The screens. You move them one at a time, in the order that matters to your business, while the rest of the Swing app keeps running in the same browser tab.

page.modernization.journey.lead.message: Each phase ships something users can see. Pick a phase to see the screen at that point and the code that makes it work.

page.modernization.talk.lead.message: A message is an action: a name, an optional string payload and an optional binary payload. The name is yours to invent. Both ends are plain Java, so nobody writes browser script for the exchange.

page.modernization.talk.announce.text.message: A double click sends {action} with the row as JSON. On the desktop the same click still opens the Swing dialog.

page.modernization.talk.reply.text.message: On save the web form sends {action} back, and the Swing app refreshes its table. Neither side calls into the other one's internals.

page.modernization.talk.send.text.message: performAction() sends a name alone or a name with data. The Swing app decides what each name means.

page.modernization.talk.ready.text.message: onInitialize fires when the connection is ready. onStart fires when the Swing app has fully loaded. Send your first action from onStart.

page.modernization.ai.lead.message: Moving screen by screen is repetitive work, and that suits an AI coding assistant. The webforJ AI plugin connects it to the webforJ MCP server and to Agent Skills, structured workflows that tell it when to use those tools, in what order, and how to validate the result.

page.modernization.start.title2.message: to a page in the browser

page.modernization.start.lead.message: You need a Swing, JavaFX or SWT app packaged as a JAR file, the Webswing server and webforJ 25.10 or later.

page.modernization.start.step1.text.message: Download Webswing, extract the archive, then start the server with the script for your platform. It answers on {url}.

page.modernization.start.step2.text.message: In the admin console at {admin}, set the application name, main class, classpath, JVM arguments and home directory. The app is then served at {url}.

page.modernization.start.step2.cors.message: Add your webforJ app's origin to Allowed Origins, for example {url}.

page.modernization.start.step2.ports.message: Both typically use 8080. Change one of them so they do not conflict.

page.modernization.start.step3.text.message: The webforj-webswing module provides WebswingConnector and the classes around it.

page.modernization.start.step4.text.message: Add a WebswingConnector to a view, as in phase 1. WebswingOptions changes its behavior, for example hiding the logout button when your webforJ app handles sign in.

page.modernization.next.lead.message: Start with a simple list and edit form. Embed the app, move that one screen to webforJ, and see how it runs next to the rest.

page.showcase.freightDispatch.useCase.message: Dispatchers give shipments to drivers and follow every truck on the road.

page.showcase.freightDispatch.descriptio.message: Operations software for a regional trucking company. Dispatchers match shipments with drivers and trucks, follow every load on the road and handle delays, all day on large screens.

page.showcase.freightDispatch.features.a.message: A side menu and header that stay in place while the work area changes.

page.showcase.freightDispatch.features.d.message: Shipment details slide in from the side, so the board stays in view.

page.showcase.freightDispatch.features.s.message: Delays and new arrival times reach every open screen from the server.

page.showcase.freightDispatch.screens.di.message: Every shipment by status, from waiting for a driver to delivered, with the numbers for today on top.

page.showcase.freightDispatch.screens.li.message: Follow every truck on the road and spot late shipments at a glance.

page.showcase.freightDispatch.screens.lo.message: Open a shipment in a side panel to see the customer, the stops and the documents.

page.showcase.freightDispatch.screens.as.message: Pick a driver by hours left, location and trailer. The app explains who fits and who does not.

page.showcase.freightDispatch.screens.de.message: Set a new arrival time, write to the customer and let the app tell them.

page.showcase.siteInspection.useCase.message: Building inspectors walk a checklist and get a sign-off, all on a phone.

page.showcase.siteInspection.description.message: Building safety inspectors follow the route for the day, walk a checklist room by room, photograph problems and get the site manager to sign off. The inspector installs it on the home screen of the phone.

page.showcase.siteInspection.features.in.message: One annotation, @AppProfile, puts the app on the home screen like a native one.

page.showcase.siteInspection.features.up.message: Photos of each problem go straight into the inspection record.

page.showcase.siteInspection.features.se.message: When the office moves an inspection, the phone shows it without a refresh.

page.showcase.siteInspection.features.ro.message: Each step, from checklist to sign-off, is its own route with a working back button.

page.showcase.siteInspection.screens.tod.message: See the route for the day, what is done and what is next. Changes from the office show up as they happen.

page.showcase.siteInspection.screens.che.message: Walk the building and mark each check as pass, fail or not applicable.

page.showcase.siteInspection.screens.rec.message: Rate how serious it is, add photos and mark them up, then set a fix-by date.

page.showcase.siteInspection.screens.ins.message: Review the score, the problems found and the notes before sign-off.

page.showcase.siteInspection.screens.sig.message: The site manager signs on the phone and the report goes out by email.

page.showcase.clinicFrontDesk.useCase.message: Reception staff check patients in, book visits and close the day.

page.showcase.clinicFrontDesk.descriptio.message: Reception at an outpatient clinic with several doctors. Staff see the whole day by clinician, check patients in, book visits, open a patient record and close the payments for the day.

page.showcase.clinicFrontDesk.features.d.message: Check-in fields are bound to the patient record and flag a bad member number as you type.

page.showcase.clinicFrontDesk.features.s.message: The waiting room updates on every desk the moment a patient checks in.

page.showcase.clinicFrontDesk.features.u.message: Referral letters and reports attach to the patient record.

page.showcase.clinicFrontDesk.features.d.message: Closing the desk asks for a clear confirmation before anything changes.

page.showcase.clinicFrontDesk.screens.to.message: The day schedule by clinician next to a waiting room that updates as patients arrive.

page.showcase.clinicFrontDesk.screens.ch.message: Find the patient, confirm their details and fix anything that does not pass the checks.

page.showcase.clinicFrontDesk.screens.bo.message: Pick a free time with the right clinician. The app warns about clashes with other visits.

page.showcase.clinicFrontDesk.screens.pa.message: Visits, documents and billing in one place, with an upload for referral letters.

page.showcase.clinicFrontDesk.screens.en.message: Check every payment and see how busy the day was before closing the desk.

page.showcase.clinicFrontDesk.screens.cl.message: Confirm what happens to open payments and bookings when the desk closes.

page.showcase.invoiceApproval.descriptio.message: Supplier invoices arrive, get checked against the purchase order, and are approved and paid by the finance team.

page.showcase.invoiceApproval.features.t.message: Filter open invoices, select several rows and approve them in one step.

page.uiComponents.hero.title1.message: Every part of a business screen,

page.uiComponents.hero.lead.message: webforJ is the full-stack Java framework for business web apps: you build the whole app, screens included, in Java. Its components cover layout, data entry, dialogs, data display and feedback, and each one is a Java class you create, configure and add to a layout.

page.uiComponents.groups.title.message: {total} business components, plus {html} HTML elements and any web component.

page.uiComponents.groups.lead.message: Pick a group, then a component. Every tile opens that component's own page in the docs.

page.uiComponents.compose.lead.message: webforJ uses composition over inheritance. You do not extend a {button}. You write a class that extends {composite}, combine components inside it, and decide which methods the rest of your app can see.

page.uiComponents.compose.point1.text.message: A {composite} wraps a single bound component and holds your internal structure, so a search bar, an address form or a whole dashboard card becomes one reusable class.

page.uiComponents.compose.point2.text.message: Callers see only the methods you expose, unlike inheritance, where everything is exposed.

page.uiComponents.compose.point3.text.message: The built-in components are final, which keeps the web component underneath consistent and predictable. Your behaviour goes around them, not into them.

page.uiComponents.beyond.title2.message: Use any component on the web.

page.uiComponents.beyond.lead.message: The business components are where you start, not where you stop. Every HTML element is a Java class, and any web component can become one.

page.uiComponents.own.lead.message: The webforJ components are an offer, not a requirement. If your design system ships as web components, you wrap it once and build the whole app with it, in Java.

page.uiComponents.own.step1.text.message: {composite} turns each custom element into a Java class and exposes its properties, attributes and events through the Java API.

page.uiComponents.own.step2.text.message: The frontend bundler lets a class declare the npm packages it needs, so the wrappers carry their design system with them. An app only adds the dependency.

page.uiComponents.own.step3.text.message: Routing, security and data binding work the same. A wrapped component that implements {valueAware} binds to your model like any built-in field.

page.uiComponents.own.panel.message: Your screens keep the look your company already designed. The framework underneath is still webforJ.

page.uiComponents.java.lead1.message: You set its state with typed methods, listen to its events with lambdas and add it to a container. The screen is Java code, with no template to keep in sync.

page.uiComponents.theme.lead.message: webforJ ships with a design system named DWC. Its CSS variables, the design tokens, cover colors, typography, borders and spacing, and every component reads them. Change a token and every component that uses it follows.

page.uiComponents.theme.lightCaption.message: The default. Light background, subtle primary-color tint.

page.uiComponents.theme.fact1.text.message: {light}, {dark} and {darkPure}, which drops the primary tint for pure neutral grays. Switch at runtime with {setTheme}, with no rebuild.

page.uiComponents.theme.fact2.text.message: Register a light and a dark theme and pass {system}. webforJ picks the one that matches the user's preference and switches again when it changes.

page.uiComponents.theme.fact3.text.message: Override the seed tokens of the built-in themes and every component picks up the new look. Shadow parts reach inside a component when a token is not enough.

page.uiComponents.entrance.lead.message: The gallery in the docs lists every component with its preview and a short description, in the same four sections the docs use.

page.uiComponents.meta.title.message: webforJ UI components: the Java component set for business apps

page.uiComponents.meta.description.message: Browse the webforJ component set by what each component does: layout, forms and inputs, data, navigation and feedback. Every component is a Java class, styled by the DWC design system and its light, dark and dark-pure themes.
